# SSH-002: Keyboard-interactive authentication is off

- **Group:** SSH
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

Keyboard-interactive authentication usually asks for the account password through PAM, so it is password authentication under another name even when PasswordAuthentication is no. It is a warning instead of a failure when a PAM second factor module is configured for sshd or AuthenticationMethods only accepts it after a key.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sudo sshd -T | grep -i '^kbdinteractiveauthentication'; grep -v '^#' /etc/pam.d/sshd
```

## How to fix it

Set KbdInteractiveAuthentication no (ChallengeResponseAuthentication on older releases) in the same early drop-in.

## What a fix can break

Logins that rely on a PAM prompt (one time codes, password through PAM) stop working; keep it only with a real second factor.

Run `stackward explain SSH-002` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
